subject: minimum sightings and segments for dsm

messages.author: d3f79de273e1d348
messages.subject: minimum sightings and segments for dsm
parts:
Dear community, 

just a simple and fast question regarding your knowledge and experience, as well as the rules that we can't violate when running a proper DSMs...
In your opinion:What is the minimum number of sightings and segments that are necessary for running a DSM?
My study area is a small reserve (9kmx7km) where different herbivores (large mammals) are kept.
I have 8 transects that I divided into 81 segments of 500m each. Each season I get around 400 sightings from different species (around 50-90 sightings per species), walking 4 times each transect.
If it's possible I would like to have more than one estimation of density per season (considering walking each transect twice), which means my sightings are reduced to less than 40. In addition some species are difficult to be seen and I have less than 40 sightings per season for some of them.
Is it suitable to estimate detection function with less than 40sightings?
Is it suitable to make a DSM with 81 segments?

What do you think? Is it impossible to increase the resolution of my study? Do i have to discard those species with less than 40?


Thank you for your help
Regards
Nicolas

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] minimum sightings and segments for dsm
parts:
Nicolás

As you know, using model-based methods of inference of density surface modelling does not provide you with the ability to use formulas for approximate amount of effort needed to achieve desired levels of precision as in section 2.4 of Buckland et al. (2015).

Nevertheless, you still need to estimate the parameters of the detection function best for your sightings--so advice in Section 2.4.1 about 60-80 sightings to estimate those parameters well still holds.  It is possible to estimate detection function parameters with fewer sightings, but reliability of that endeavour is more down to luck.  With small numbers of detections, inclusion/exclusion of a couple of detections near the transect may have profound consequences for the shape of the estimated detection function -- and consequently the estimated number of animals in the non-empty segments.

To produce reliable inference from your model-based estimates from data in your 81 segments is harder to judge.  The quality of this inference depends upon the proportion of those segments where there were detections as well as the quality of the explanatory model fitted--which is contingent upon the predictor variables used and their explanatory power.

Sorry the answer is vague, but that is the nature of sample size determination with model-based inference.
